subject: CurieBank production: dedicated pool backpressure + error spike
messages:
From: Leah O'Connor <leah.oconnor@curiebank.com>
To: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.example>
Cc: David Li <david.li@curiebank.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Nov 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Production errors and latency (CurieBank)

Aditya —

We're seeing a sharp degradation in CurieBank's production profile starting ~08:45 PST. Symptoms: p95 generation latency jumped from ~120ms to >1.2s, and 5xx error rate climbed from ~0.1% to ~3.8% across the last 15 minutes. Our traffic is routed to the dedicated pool you provisioned under the reserved contract. Throughput to our endpoints is also throttling — QPS is lower than our committed baseline despite sustained load.

We've attached a short log sample and a CSV of QPS by minute. Can you triage urgently and advise:
- Is this an issue on your side (GPU saturation / scheduling) or something in the model variant?
- How long until normal service is restored?
- If you need us to shift traffic, what's the recommended fallback (hosted variant, smaller batch size)?

This is impacting payment routing. We need an estimate within 15 minutes and an interim mitigation.

Attached: curiebank_error_samples.log, curiebank_qps_trend.csv

— Leah
Leah O'Connor
Product Lead, ML Platform
CurieBank

From: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.example>
To: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.example>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.example>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example>
Cc: Leah O'Connor <leah.oconnor@curiebank.com>, David Li <david.li@curiebank.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Nov 2027 09:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production errors and latency (CurieBank)

Thanks for flagging, Leah — we're on it.

Triage notes (initial):
- Observed elevated GPU utilization on the dedicated pool serving CurieBank (nodes in pool at 96%+).
- Telemetry shows KV cache churn correlated with longer conversation sequences from CurieBank's recent release (sequence length distribution shifted right). That increases per-request memory pressure and can trigger backpressure and batching slowdowns.
- We see increased queue latency and a rise in request timeouts that surface as 5xx on the customer side.

Immediate mitigation plan (executing now):
1) Provision two emergency burst GPU instances and attach to CurieBank's pool (warm nodes, fast path).
2) Temporarily reroute a portion of CurieBank traffic to a warmed fallback pool with tuned batch-window=8 and max-batch-latency=20ms.
3) Enable prefix caching stricter-eviction to reduce KV churn for the heavy sequences.
4) If errors persist, fall back to the quantized-compatible model variant (lower memory) for non-critical routes.

Monica — can you run the provisioning and confirm when burst nodes are joined? Add the QPS trend to the ticket.
Vivek/Marissa — I'm going to need an exec note and customer comms draft.

Leah/David — will follow up in ~15–20 minutes with status. Apologies for the disruption — we'll take ownership on incident communications and a root-cause postmortem.

— Aditya
Aditya Rao
Senior Account Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.example>
To: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.example>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.example>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example>, Leah O'Connor <leah.oconnor@curiebank.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Nov 2027 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production errors and latency (CurieBank)

On Mon, Nov 1, 2027 at 09:25 AM aditya_rao wrote:
> Monica — can you run the provisioning and confirm when burst nodes are joined? Add the QPS trend to the ticket.

Provisioning update:
- Two burst instances (A100-like) launched and joined pool at 09:36. Warmup completed ~09:39.
- Reduced server-side batch window and max-stack latency applied to CurieBank route at 09:40.
- Enabled stricter prefix eviction policy at 09:41.

Outcome so far: error rate dropped from peak 3.8% to ~1.9%. p95 latency improving but still elevated (~720ms). Throughput recovering slowly; we see QPS stabilize but still below contract baseline during peak minutes. Attached the live QPS dump: curiebank_qps_trend.csv.

Next steps I'm executing:
- Start gradual routing of 30% of traffic to quantized fallback variant (non-critical predictions) to further relieve memory pressure.
- Keep monitoring for eviction storms; if we see any node OOMs we'll spin additional burst nodes.

Leah — attaching raw error snippets for visibility (excerpt). If you want us to switch all traffic to fallback now, say the word — this will reduce cost/unit quality slightly but should restore latency quickly.

— Monica
Monica Patel
SRE, Redwood Inference

From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.example>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.example>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.example>
Cc: Leah O'Connor <leah.oconnor@curiebank.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Nov 2027 10:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Escalation: CurieBank - executive attention requested

Folks — looping in leadership for visibility. CurieBank is a priority account and the degradation is material to payment flows.

Summary: dedicated pool hit sustained high utilization because of a shift in sequence lengths causing persistent KV cache churn and slower batching. We've provisioned burst capacity and begun routing to a quantized fallback for non-critical routes. Error rate improved but not fully back to SLO.

Immediate asks:
- Marissa: please prepare a short customer note (2–3 bullets) offering the following: 1) apology + incident acknowledgement, 2) mitigations performed and ETA for stabilization (15–45 minutes window), 3) offer a one-day service credit and a commitment for a postmortem within 48 hours. Draft attached: draft_customer_note_v1.txt.
- Aditya: confirm whether we should perform a full failover to the hosted-compatible variant (impact to quality) if QPS doesn't reach baseline by 11:15.
- Monica: continue monitoring; if p95 does not drop below 300ms within 30 minutes, prep to spin two more burst nodes.

I'll join the bridge at 10:45. If anyone from sales/legal needs to be looped (procurement@curiebank.com), do so now.

— Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Customer Success, Redwood Inference
From: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.example>
To: Leah O'Connor <leah.oconnor@curiebank.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.example>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.example>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example>
Date: Tue, 2 Nov 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: CurieBank incident update and next steps

Leah —

Thank you again for your patience. Quick summary and next steps following today's incident: 

What we did (executed):
- Provisioned two burst GPU instances and joined CurieBank's dedicated pool.
- Tuned batching and enabled stricter prefix eviction to reduce KV churn.
- Gradual routing to a quantized fallback for lower-criticality routes; full-quality routes remained on the primary variant.

What's happening now:
- We saw p95 latency fall from the high 1s to ~220–320ms over the span of the evening after additional warmups. Error rate is back under 0.5% for critical routes. Overall QPS is trending back toward your committed baseline.

Compensation & follow-up:
- We're prepared to apply a one-day service credit (per Vivek's note) and will send the formal SLA credit note after you confirm.
- We're scheduling a joint RCA with your team within 48 hours; proposed windows attached. We'll include mitigation work (KV cache heuristics, routing policy adjustments, and a long-term plan to avoid saturation during sequence-length distribution shifts).

Operational ask: with your permission we'd like to run a short controlled synthetic load test next week (with your team in the loop) to validate the new routing and warm-pool behavior. This will help make sure a similar shift doesn't reoccur.

If you'd like immediate full failover to the hosted-compatible model while the RCA completes, we can enact that (expect modest quality delta). Please confirm preference.

Apologies again for the interruption — we own this and will provide a detailed postmortem.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Senior Account Engineer, Redwood Inference
